text:
You've got the first part of the idea right: an object in motion will stay in motion. Nicely done.

The second part, "Force makes things keep moving," is a really common misconception. Force is actually what *changes* an object's motion — making it speed up, slow down, or change direction. An object moving in a straight line at a constant speed has no net force acting on it.

You also missed one part of the law: objects at rest stay at rest.

So, a more complete statement is:
> An object at rest stays at rest, and an object in motion stays in motion with the same speed and in the same direction, unless acted upon by an unbalanced external force.

Here's a question for you: If you slide a hockey puck across a perfectly smooth, endless sheet of ice, does it need a continuous force to keep moving? Why or why not?

updates.reason: Misconception that force sustains motion rather than changing it.
